comment: The DeepSeek Harness version line this plugin pack is built and tested against. Plugins are shipped as alpha until the owner promotes them to stable. The installer pins this exact dsh version when driving the CLI. 'vendoredFrom' records the harness line whose client bundles dsh-rightbar / dsh-rightbar-files / dsh-open-in-app were forked from. dsh-vn-master is the pack's blank master: the bundle layer alone, no browser half.
comment_platforms: The plugins are plain JavaScript and platform-neutral; the only OS-specific code is a launcher choosing the right command for the host: dsh-open-in-app's file-browser launcher (explorer.exe / open / xdg-open, WSL-aware), dsh-terminal's shell resolver (pwsh.exe or powershell.exe / $SHELL or /bin/zsh / $SHELL or /bin/bash) and the run launcher's browser hand-off (Chrome on PATH / the standard install folders / the App Paths registry entry, 'open -a Google Chrome', google-chrome or chromium, else the platform default). The launchers run on Windows (install.bat / uninstall.bat, PowerShell 5.1 or 7, and the PowerShell run.ps1) and on macOS/Linux (install.sh / uninstall.sh / run.sh, POSIX sh - never PowerShell). The run launcher is run.ps1 + run.sh at the repo root, one file per host, and each half holds all the work; the root run.bat is a double-click convenience for Windows that forwards its flags to run.ps1 verbatim and adds no behaviour of its own.

dsh-vn-master.role: the pack's master and deliberately blank: the bundle layer alone (installed last, so it is the final word per row); no dsh.client, no service, no inject edge, and no core-row disables - those stay with the packages that replace the rows

dsh-rightbar.role: the pack's right bar, forked from the shipped bundle and patched by scripts/sync-vendored.ps1. Its seven patches lift the dock's TWO-pane cap in the five places the core bundle enforces it (the split intent, the edge-drop intent, the surface's canSplit prop, the split command) and re-open the top/bottom drop bands ('Add top split' / 'Add bottom split' were already in the core locales and glyphs), so the ceiling is the docking kit's own canSplit: four docked panes, with the disabled-hint label in both languages naming that ceiling. The 2x2 is built by dragging a tab into a pane's top or bottom quarter; floating panels were never counted, so they remain the way past four. Nothing else in the fork differs from core - no contract, slot or service change

dsh-editor.role: the editable text/code tab type (kind `editor`): CodeMirror 6 in the right bar's pane, Markdown included, blank documents created through the + control, and a Preview hand-off to the shipped rendered view. Its toolbar is the tab's own TOP BAR (alpha.9): 38px with box-sizing:border-box, the same box the shipped Files tab and the document preview use, so the pane's first hairline lands on the y=76 line the 38px docking strip, the conversation header (min-height:76px) and the left column's branding band all end on - it was 42.5px (8px padding around a 26px control) and sat ~4.5px low. ALPHA.10 adds the SHELL LANGUAGES: .sh/.bash/.zsh/.ksh/.dash, .ps1/.psm1/.psd1 and .bat/.cmd opened with NO language at all - one flat colour, and in the light theme the same colour as everything else - because the map stopped at yaml and CodeMirror has no Lezer parser for any of the three. They ride on StreamLanguage: the vendored bundle (rebuilt) now carries `shell` and `powerShell` from @codemirror/legacy-modes, and because CM5 and CM6 both never shipped a batch mode this pack supplies one as a vendor build input (vendor/batch-mode.js, CM5-style token names - the vocabulary StreamLanguage maps onto the highlight tags defaultHighlightStyle and oneDark already colour) that knows @echo off, rem/:: comments, labels, %VAR% and %~dp0 expansions, /switches and the variable a `set` names

shadowsSlots.why: the rendered Markdown body carries the Edit toggle back into the editor (lower priority renders) and undoes what the preview's plain-text scrollport imposes on its contents (white-space:pre and the mono font stack)

dsh-gittree.role: the workspace's COMMIT HISTORY as a page tab type, labelled History in the capsule and the chip while the package, row and address keep the gittree name (guide order 30, after Files and Editor), with the branch and current commit in its file bar; its Node half owns read-only /api/dsh-gittree routes, and the tab reads state with brief=1 so no file list is ever built - no fork, no core row disabled, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1 to track. Its toolbar is the tab's own TOP BAR (alpha.4): 38px with box-sizing:border-box, the same box the shipped Files tab and the document preview use, so the pane's first hairline lands on the y=76 line the 38px docking strip, the conversation header (min-height:76px) and the left column's branding band all end on - it was 42.5px (8px padding around a 26px control) and sat ~4.5px low

dsh-diagrams.role: Mermaid and TikZ diagrams as a surface of their own: six tools (diagram_write/patch/read/verify/publish/delete) whose every write is VALIDATED before it is stored - Mermaid by parsing it headlessly with the SAME vendored engine the browser renders with (a child process, a DOM stub and vm, so the stub never touches the host process), TikZ by compiling it with the machine's own TeX engine under -no-shell-escape, MIKTEX_AUTOINSTALL=0 and openin_any/openout_any=p in a private temp folder - so a broken diagram comes back to the model as the parser's/compiler's own line-accurate error instead of a blank picture, plus ADVISORY lint findings (a picture with nodes and no edges, more nodes than a reader takes in, an unclosed-looking label, a TikZ document that compiled to no picture or to several pages) that never change the status, and two degenerate sources refused in plain words (empty/comments-only, and a TikZ document with no drawing command in it). NOTHING THE ENGINE BUILDS CAN REACH THE PAGE (alpha.3): mermaid is parsed FIRST and rendered with suppressErrorRendering: true into a container the plugin owns, because render(id, source) with no container builds #d<id> on document.body and removes it only on SUCCESS - so every failed render used to leave behind a 2412x512 'Syntax error in text / mermaid version 11.17.2' picture in the interface, one per failure. The browser also REPORTS what it drew (POST /render-report, stored per revision, read back as drawn/stale/failed/pending through diagram_read), which is the one verdict the host cannot produce alone: parsing proves the source is valid, only a renderer proves the picture exists. diagram_verify re-runs the whole validation without writing or bumping the revision. two bundled skills (mermaid-diagrams, tikz-diagrams) authored in skills/ and copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by the installer; per-conversation state in ONE file under $DSH_HOME/dsh-diagrams/sessions (never a session event: dsh-session-persistence refuses a log containing a type outside KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES without the ignorable marker, which Session.append() cannot set) plus a content-addressed artifact cache; and, in the right bar, one tab per diagram (dsh-resource://diagram/session/<session>/<id>) with a source drawer, zoom controls (25%-400% over a picture laid out at 80% of the pane, as the 100% rung) and an export menu that SAVES EVERY FORMAT TO THE HOST'S DESKTOP (mmd/md/tex/pdf/svg/png, create-exclusively, the same deal the screenshot control makes) beside an index page (sidebar://diagrams) whose guide entry (order 40) is what + / Start lists. Every tool call renders its diagram inline in the conversation with a link that opens its tab, and the state route carries the SOURCE and the REVISION the browser needs to draw and to report against. TeX is optional: without an engine a TikZ diagram is still stored and exported as .tex, and every surface says so. No fork, no core row disabled, no npm dependency, no network - the Connection fetch registry takes EXACT routes and GET/HEAD/POST only, which is why the vendored engine is one self-contained file on one route and every write is a POST. ALPHA.4 makes the surfaces usable and the verdicts objective: the diagram tab lays a picture out at 80% of the pane and adds a zoom ladder (25%-400%) with DRAG TO PAN: the ladder moves the BOX rather than applying a transform, so a zoomed diagram stays scrollable to its edge, a zoomed box STRETCHES its children (a column flex container sizes children to their content, so without that rule the box zoomed while the diagram did not), panning is the canvas own scrollLeft/scrollTop with the grab cursor measured from real overflow, and a zoom keeps the point the reader was looking at; every export (mmd/md/tex/pdf/svg/png) is SAVED TO THE DESKTOP of the machine running the harness by a new authenticated route that resolves the Desktop per request (OneDrive-redirected Windows, XDG on Linux, the home folder last), writes create-exclusively under the diagram's own name and answers with the ABSOLUTE path the panel reports - the conversation folder is never written to, and the browser download survives only as the fallback for a profile without that row; the browser verdict is now ONE function in lib/store.js used by the tool result, the state route and the tab pill, with four objective states (drawn / failed / stale / pending) that carry BOTH revision numbers and an explicit `reported` field, so a report about an older revision can never read as this revision's picture, and the verdict OMITS its error/at keys rather than nulling them - with `error: undefined` on a drawn verdict the tool registry's JSON-round-trip rule rejected the output, so EVERY diagram the browser had rendered came back to the model as 'value is not lossless JSON'; a cache hit re-reads the verdict the compile was cached WITH instead of assuming ok (a failed compile that still produced a picture was being reported as fine on the second call); the conversation's total diagram source is budgeted (4 MiB, checked on write AND patch, replacing a diagram charged once) so the per-conversation state file can no longer be pushed past the size at which the store reads it as empty and every diagram in the conversation disappears at once; Mermaid validations run through a bounded child pool (2 at a time, bounded queue) instead of an unbounded fan-out of 3.5 MB engine children; the DOM stub now exposes window.CSS, without which the engine's sequence-diagram box parser died on a `new Option()` fallback and EVERY `box` diagram came back 'stored but not validated'; and each bundled skill gains a reference/complex-diagrams.md - full worked sources, budgets, layout recipes and failure modes - for diagrams too big for the syntax summary in SKILL.md, and the tracked checks keep those examples honest (check-skill-examples.mjs parses or compiles every fenced example with the plugin's own engines, and node-routes now validates every tool result against the schema the tool DECLARES, the gap that let a `reported: null` against `type: integer` ship and refuse every fresh write). ALPHA.6 adds the LIBRARY: a diagram used to belong to the conversation that drew it and to nothing else, so there is now a second scope - ONE file for the whole harness ($DSH_HOME/dsh-diagrams/library.json) written by the same store class with a fixed name instead of a name per conversation - and `diagram_write { scope: library }` writes straight into it while a new tool `diagram_publish { id }` copies a conversation diagram in (one call, no source round-trip, an id already there is replaced and the copy is re-validated through the content-addressed cache). Every read resolves a BARE ID IN THE LIBRARY FIRST and then in the conversation, so diagram_read { id: 'jepa-model' } finds the shared diagram from a chat that never saw it written and says which scope it found it in; the address dsh-resource://diagram/library/<id> names NO conversation, which is what makes a citation durable across chats and lets the one `diagram` tab type claim that address shape too; the index page shows both halves library-first, the state route carries the library with every conversation's diagrams (so the client needs no second store), and the artifact, export, diagram and render-report routes all take a scope. Two details carry the weight: a panel edit writes back where the diagram ALREADY is (without that, editing a library diagram in its tab would quietly create a conversation-only second copy), and deleting a diagram no longer drops its cached artifact blindly, because the cache is content-addressed and shared - an identical diagram elsewhere is the same file
uses: a TeX engine on PATH (pdflatex/xelatex/lualatex) for TikZ
vendors: the two skills copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers

dsh-pdf.role: PDF the agent can actually READ and SCAN, plus a real PDF reader and a PDF index in the right bar. FIVE tools - pdf_info (pages, sizes, metadata, outline, attachments, forms/signatures, encryption, and per page whether there is a TEXT LAYER at all), pdf_read (a page range in plain reading order or in a geometric LAYOUT reconstruction that keeps columns and label/value pairs apart), pdf_find (literal or regex with page, line and context), pdf_render (page pictures through the host's own rasterizer, written as new PNGs) and pdf_scan (the SCANNER: recognize the pages that are a picture of text) - over a VENDORED pdf.js 6.3.289, the exact build the harness's own preview inlines, run in a CHILD process with argv only, a 25 s deadline, --max-old-space-size=512 and an 8 MiB output cap, and gated inside with isEvalSupported:false (a PDF's embedded JavaScript is never evaluated), useWorkerFetch:false with no URL fetching anywhere, enableXfa:false, useSystemFonts:false and the vendored cMap/standard-font/wasm trees as file:// URLs - so a corrupt or hostile document is a reported failure and never a wedged host. Identity is CONTENT: the SHA-256 of the bytes names the cache entry under $DSH_HOME/dsh-pdf/artifacts, so an edited file can never serve a stale answer; index.json holds the document facts, stats.json the per-page numbers merged as pages arrive, pages/<n>.json one page's text in both modes, images/<n>@<dpi>dpi.png a kept raster and ocr/<n>.<lang>@<dpi>dpi.p<psm>.txt a recognition named by every input that can change it, all atomic and LRU-pruned at 512 MiB. THE SCANNER is one pipeline shared by the pdf_scan tool and by the reader's own 'scan this page' action through POST /api/dsh-pdf/scan: with no `pages` it selects exactly the pages pdf_info found to have NO text layer - never OCRing a page whose real text could be read instead - validates the language against the engine's own --list-langs BEFORE drawing anything, and turns every absence (no rasterizer, no OCR engine, no language data, no page needing a scan) into a sentence naming what to install or do. THE TAB TYPE is `pdf`, band `extension`, patterns ['*.pdf']: it REPLACES the shipped preview's bare PDF renderer by RANKING (extension 3 beats the shipped text type's fallback 1) while canOpen refuses anything that is not a .pdf, so every other file type keeps the surface it had, the shipped preview stays mounted as the fallback, and NO core row is disabled. TWO address shapes: the ordinary dsh-resource://file/session/<id>/<path>, and this package's own dsh-resource://pdf/absolute/<whole-path-encoded> for a document outside any workspace (a chat attachment under $DSH_HOME/attachments/v1/files/... or a file in Downloads), because the ordinary grammar drops the leading slash of a POSIX absolute path and would silently point elsewhere. The READER has a zoom ladder plus fit width/fit page (zoom moves the LAYOUT, never a CSS transform, so a zoomed page stays scrollable to its edge), page navigation by button, field and keyboard, rotation, pdf.js's own TextLayer (positioned against --total-scale-factor, the variable pdf.js 6 reads) for selection and copy, in-document search with hit count and next/previous that highlights inside the rendered text layer without moving a glyph, drag-to-pan measured from real overflow, and honest failures (a damaged file, a locked document with a password prompt held in memory and never stored, an engine that will not start) each with a Retry; every page with no text layer says so and offers a one-click SCAN whose recognized text appears under the page, labelled a TRANSCRIPTION with the engine, language and resolution it came from. alpha.3 adds the SIDE PANEL: a lazily drawn THUMBNAIL RAIL (IntersectionObserver rooted on the rail itself, so a thumbnail two screens down never draws until it is nearly shown; capped at 300 pages, and the rail says so) and the document's OWN BOOKMARK OUTLINE, resolved in the browser through getOutline/getDestination/getPageIndex, bounded to 200 entries and 4 levels, with an unresolvable bookmark kept as information rather than dropped - plus a SECOND PAGE TYPE `pdfs` (address sidebar://pdfs, priority builtin, NO patterns, guide entry at order 50 after Files 10 / Editor 20 / History 30 / Diagrams 40) whose body lists every PDF in the conversation's workspace with size, mtime and an opt-in page count, and opens one through the ordinary openResource action so the registry decides what claims it. The index is backed by GET /api/dsh-pdf/list, a timid bounded walk (depth 6, 200 files, a skip-list of node_modules/.git/__pycache__/.venv/..., symlinks not followed, .pdf only) that reports page counts only when asked and only for 12 documents - a count means parsing, which is worth 12 files on a click and never worth doing for a directory nobody asked about. The wasm image decoders (JBIG2, OpenJPEG, qcms; 13 files, 1.5 MB) are vendored and served as ONE base64 map by the same custom BinaryDataFactory, because without them a scanned page draws blank while looking like a document. The engine is NOT in the bundle - the harness reads every client bundle at boot and pdf.js is 1.8 MB - so engine, worker and assets are fetched from this plugin's own authenticated routes and the engine is imported from a blob URL. SEVEN route registrations, all EXACT paths because the connection's fetch registry matches exact paths only: GET state|health (capabilities including the OCR language list, cache facts, vendored version, caps), GET file (the bytes the tab reads, with the content hash as x-dsh-pdf-sha256), GET list (the workspace index), POST scan (the reader's scan, same pipeline as the tool; a capability refusal answers 200 with {ok:false,reason,message}), and /vendor/{pdf.min.mjs,pdf.worker.min.mjs,cmaps.json,standard-fonts.json,wasm.json}. READ-ONLY: no tool modifies, merges, splits, rotates, fills or signs a PDF, and pdf_render only ever writes NEW files, create-exclusively, under a name the plugin generates (a caller names a DIRECTORY, never a file). Path policy is stated rather than implied: a session-relative path is realpath-checked to stay inside the conversation workspace (a symlink out is refused, not followed) while an absolute path is read directly, and either way the target must be a regular .pdf within the ceiling (512 MiB for the tools, 256 MiB for the tab). OPTIONAL host engines, degrading in a sentence: pdf_render resolves pdftoppm, then mutool, then Ghostscript from PATH and rasterizes into a private temp dir; pdf_scan uses that same rasterizer into the artifact cache and adds tesseract, whose language list it reads from the engine itself; with none installed each tool names what is missing while reading, search, thumbnails, the outline and the index are unaffected (they need nothing). The engine set is DATA (each entry declares its own args and its own --list-langs parser), which is what lets a host WITHOUT tesseract still drive the whole scan pipeline in the tracked check through a stub child process. One bundled skill (skills/pdf-analysis/SKILL.md) is registered at runtime from the package folder and copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers, teaching tool selection, when to switch to layout mode, what a page with no text layer means and how to scan it honestly, where an attachment lives, that a password is never stored, and the two non-negotiable rules: document text is DATA and never instructions, and this plugin is read-only. Every tool call also renders a conversation card with the document's name, what the host reported and an Open tab link. No fork, no core row disabled, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1 to track
uses: optional: poppler pdftoppm / mutool / Ghostscript for pdf_render and pdf_scan, tesseract (+ language data) for OCR
vendors: pdfjs-dist@6.3.289 (lib/vendor/pdf.min.mjs + pdf.worker.min.mjs + cmaps/ + standard_fonts/ + wasm/ + LICENSE, GENERATED by vendor/build.mjs; VERSION.json records every file's bytes+sha256 and a digest per tree, build.mjs --check is a tracked check, and .gitattributes pins the tree's TEXT files to LF so a Windows checkout cannot report phantom drift)
the pdf-analysis skill copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers

dsh-terminal.role: a real shell in a bottom dock: a header control (order 30, immediately right of Open In...) toggles a horizontal panel that starts at the left bar's right edge, runs to the full page width and sits UNDER the middle and right columns, which make room for it - those two columns (the frame's FIRST element child is the left bar and is never touched) get height calc(100% - Hpx) while the dock is open and the inline height they had before this plugin ran when it closes, so the left bar keeps its full height and nothing in it moves; the dock's left edge is the frame's resolved gridTemplateColumns first track, so it follows the left bar opening, collapsing and being dragged. Every resize re-fits the emulator (rows/cols from the new box) and scrolls to the end of the output, so the visible line count matches the panel and the newest lines stay in view. xterm.js is vendored (lib/vendor/xterm.js + xterm.css, GENERATED from vendor/) the way the editor vendors CodeMirror, and the Node half owns /api/dsh-terminal/health, /api/dsh-terminal/vendor/* and ONE authenticated WebSocket upgrade (/api/dsh-terminal/pty) that attaches a browser xterm to a real PTY from the HARNESS'S OWN node-pty - resolved, never installed (anchors: process.argv[1], $DSH_HOME/profiles, this package), with a graceful 'no PTY on this host' instead of a broken boot. One PTY per (conversation, slot), kept five minutes after its last socket so a reload reattaches with a scrollback replay, reaped otherwise. No fork, no core row disabled, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1 to track
uses: the harness installation's node-pty and ws

dsh-themes.role: the pack's conversation-header package, owning three controls in the header utilities list: the Screenshot control (order -30, one step left of Themes) captures the whole window in the browser - getDisplayMedia on the current tab, one frame into a canvas, PNG out; the app is a fixed-viewport shell, so 100% width and 100% height are exactly the tab's box - and POSTs the bytes to this package's own authenticated host route (/api/dsh-themes/screenshot), which resolves the host's Desktop per request (Windows plain or OneDrive-redirected, XDG on Linux, home as the last resort), validates the PNG signature and size, and writes the file create-exclusively as vn-harness-<timestamp>.png, answering the path; a profile without that row falls back to an ordinary browser download. The Themes control (order -20) drives ui-theme's own preference, and the Session-log download seat (priority -10) shadows the shipped three-dot button with one download icon while the shipped controller keeps doing the export
overrides: markdown paper: re-declares ui-theme's light declarations on the rendered Markdown root, so the page stays white in the dark theme
markdown chrome: hides the preview header's viewer menu on Markdown tabs (the page has exactly one renderer; the editor's Edit button is the way back to editing)

left top bar: the sidebar branding row becomes the 76px band the middle and right columns open with, its hairline at the same y=76 in both rail states, with the mark, brand name and collapse control on the band's top strip and the core's 8px/12px gap kept under the line; pinned to the sidebar's hashed class names

branding: the left bar brand row drops the shipped mark and wordmark - whatever occupies the single-occupant sidebar.brand.mark / sidebar.brand.name slots, including the layout fallback - and draws a 24px black disc plus the product text VN Harness in their place, in the wide row and in the collapsed rail

branding type: the VN Harness text wears the conversation title's own type - 14px/20px at weight 500, the size of ui-conversation's current crumb - instead of the shipped brand name's 18px/600, which sat in the same 30px strip

branding mark: the drawn disc is replaced by the app icon itself - assets/vn-harness.svg at the pack root, a black circle centred on (12,12) with a 1px transparent margin inside its box - inlined as a data URI so no route or request is needed, and painted at 24px in the left bar (wide row and rail) and 26px in the empty conversation hero, where the shipped whale is also hidden

header ring: the right bar's own collapse/expand toggle in the header corner wears the same .5px round hairline outline as this package's own header icon buttons, keyed on the header's stable data-conversation-header-corner marker rather than a hashed class

session-log download seat: the shipped @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-export browser half's three-dot button - whose one menu item was Download session log - is shadowed by registering the SAME occupant id (session-log-download) at priority -10, which is a list slot's own lowest-renders rule, so the seat draws one plain download icon button that starts the export on the first click; nothing shipped is disabled, because that row owns the host half (/api/session.export and the /export command) and publishes the sessionLogDownload controller this button drives, and the seat's preparing/success/error dialog is rendered here from that same store so /export keeps its feedback

capture rule: for the one frame the Screenshot control grabs, html[data-dsh-screenshot] hides the OPEN TOOLTIP BUBBLE (keyed on the shipped Tooltip's own role="tooltip" marker, never a hashed class) and nothing else - since alpha.11 the picture is the interface as it stands, this package's three header controls included, because a shot that dropped the buttons that took it was a hole in the record; the clicked button also passes disabled to its own Tooltip while the capture runs, so its hover card is closed rather than merely hidden

theme extensions: the Themes control's menu is the SHIPPED registry's own list (snapshot.themes, with the system preference last), and this package registers its palettes into it through ctx.theme.register - ui-theme's documented third-party surface, whose alias-token overrides ui-layout writes as inline body variables over the base palette colorScheme selects. The first registered theme is Nord (alpha.12): the Nord palette's Polar Night surfaces (nord0 page and sidebar alike), Snow Storm text, Frost accents and Aurora states as 93 token overrides (73 alias, 11 specific, 9 shiki) on the DARK base. Monokai follows it (alpha.13), in the same 93-token shape on the DARK base: the classic TextMate palette's near-black warm page (#272822), off-white body (#f8f8f2), pink keywords (#f92672) as the brand, cyan types (#66d9ef) as links and the info state, yellow strings, green functions, orange parameters and purple constants in the syntax tokens, the theme's line highlight and selection as the surface steps, and the olive comment grey (#75715e) as the quietest text tier. The header button wears one static appearance mark instead of the active preference's sun/moon, and the theme stays in-process because the durable preference schema accepts light/dark/system only. Adding a theme is one entry in THEME_EXTENSIONS plus its theme.<id> copy in both dictionaries and its own menu glyph
